verses.11:2: Salvai-me, Senhor, porque {defecit}: * porque {diminutae} entre os filhos dos homens.
verses.11:5: Os que disseram: Engrandeceremos a nossa língua, † {anobis}, * {dominus}?
verses.11:6a: {propter} e do gemido dos pobres, * agora me levantarei, diz o Senhor.
verses.11:8: Vós, Senhor, {servabis} * desta geração para sempre.
verses.11:9: Os ímpios andam ao redor: * segundo a vossa {altitudinem} multiplicastes os filhos dos homens.

decisions.why: defícere: to fail, give out, cease; the Greek ἐκλέλοιπεν ‘has failed, is gone’. The subject is ‘sanctus’ (ὅσιος, the godly man; glossary: sanctus → santo, Ps 4), singular for the kind. The glossary’s working verb for defícere is ‘desfalecer’ (Ps 118:81 …), which here would say that the holy man fainted. Douay-Rheims ‘for there is now no saint’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘porque não se encontra um homem de bem’ (explains).

options.label: desapareceu o santo
options.note: Ruling: the Greek’s and Lewis & Short’s ‘cease, come to an end’, said of a person as Portuguese says it; ‘santo’ keeps the glossary word for ὅσιος. The subject after the verb, as the Latin has it.

options.label: já não há santo
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘there is now no saint’; the state that follows the event, and ‘já’ supplied.

options.label: acabou-se o santo
options.note: Colloquial; can be heard as ‘holiness is over’.

options.label: desfaleceu o santo
options.note: The glossary’s verb for defícere. Refused here: it says the holy man fainted.

decisions.latin: quóniam diminútæ sunt veritátes a fíliis hóminum
decisions.why: A passive perfect with middle sense (the Greek ὠλιγώθησαν, ‘became few’); veritátes is plural (αἱ ἀλήθειαι) and stays plural (glossary: véritas → verdade); ‘a fíliis hóminum’ is ‘from among’ (ἀπό). Douay-Rheims ‘truths are decayed from among the children of men’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘as verdades (já) não são apreciadas entre os filhos dos homens’ (another sense). diminúere is only here in the psalter (grep).

options.label: diminuíram as verdades
options.note: Ruling: the cognate, intransitive, for a passive with middle sense (as Ps 8:2b ‘se elevou’); the plural kept; ‘entre’ for ‘a’ (Matos Soares 1932).

options.label: minguaram as verdades
options.note: ‘Minguar’ is the waning of the moon: concrete, and exactly ‘became few’. A shade literary.

options.label: foram diminuídas as verdades
options.note: The passive to the letter; it asks by whom.

decisions.latin: Vana locúti sunt unusquísque ad próximum suum
decisions.why: A plural verb with ‘unusquísque’ in apposition; the Greek has a singular verb here and a plural in the second colon (ἐλάλησεν ἕκαστος … ἐλάλησαν). vana (neuter plural) → ‘coisas vãs’ (glossary: inánia → coisas vãs; vánitas keeps ‘vaidade’). loqui → falar. próximus → ‘próximo’, a proparoxytone, cannot stand at the mediant (rule 4), where the Latin has ‘suum’. Douay-Rheims ‘They have spoken vain things every one to his neighbour’.

options.label: Cada um falou ao seu próximo coisas vãs

forms.vana: Cada um falou ao seu próximo coisas vãs

options.note: Ruling: the mediant falls on the oxytone ‘vãs’; ‘cada um’ takes the singular verb Portuguese gives it (the Greek’s number; the Latin’s plural returns in the second colon, ‘falaram’). The object after the indirect object puts ‘coisas vãs’ where the stress of the colon falls.

options.label: Falaram coisas vãs, cada um ao seu próximo

forms.vana: Falaram coisas vãs, cada um ao seu próximo

options.note: The Latin’s plural verb, apposition and order, and the frame falaram … falaram; but the mediant falls on the proparoxytone ‘próximo’ (rule 4).

options.label: Cada um falou vaidades ao seu próximo

forms.vana: Cada um falou vaidades ao seu próximo

options.note: ‘Vaidade’ is vánitas’s word (glossary), and is heard as conceit.

decisions.why: Glossary: dolus / dolósus → engano / enganador (open, Ps 5), which names ‘lábia dolósa 11:3–4’. The phrase is said twice, in consecutive verses, and says the same twice here. The cognate ‘doloso’ is criminal law in Brazil (Matos Soares 1932 ‘lábios dolosos’).

options.label: enganadores
options.note: Ruling: the glossary’s adjective, both times.

options.label: enganosos
options.note: Of the thing rather than the agent (lips that deceive / deceptive lips); the glossary keeps ‘enganador’.

options.label: dolosos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. A term of criminal law today.

decisions.latin: lábia dolósa, in corde et corde locúti sunt
decisions.why: ‘in corde et corde’ is the Hebrew idiom for a double heart, carried word for word by the Greek (ἐν καρδίᾳ καὶ ἐν καρδίᾳ) and the Latin: the figure is the repetition. Douay-Rheims ‘with a double heart’ and Matos Soares 1932 ‘com coração dúplice’ explain it. ‘lábia dolósa’ stands without a preposition in the Latin (the Greek has a nominative); Portuguese supplies ‘com’, as Douay-Rheims does, so that the lips are not heard as the subject of ‘falaram’ (the Latin’s masculine ‘locúti’ excludes it).

options.label: com coração e coração
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s figure kept, not explained (rule 2); the second ‘com’ answers the first (com lábios …, com coração …). To be tested on the blind reader.

options.label: com um coração e outro coração

forms.corde: com um coração e outro coração

options.note: The repetition kept and the doubleness made plain by ‘um … outro’; two words supplied.

options.label: com duplo coração
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘double heart’ (and the Diurnal’s ‘duplo coração’): the sense, but the figure explained.

options.label: com coração dúplice
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Explains, and ends the colon on a proparoxytone before the verb.

decisions.why: Glossary: dispérdere → exterminar (working, Ps 53:7; ‘destruir’ is destrúere’s and fails at the vós imperative). A jussive subjunctive with the subject after it.

options.label: Extermine o Senhor
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb, the subject after it as the Latin has it — natural for a Portuguese jussive.

options.label: Que o Senhor extermine
options.note: The wish marked by ‘que’; one syllable more.

options.label: Destrua o Senhor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. ‘Destruir’ is destrúere’s (glossary).

decisions.why: magníloquus: ‘in a bad sense, that speaks in a pompous style, vaunting, boastful’ (Lewis & Short, citing this verse); the Greek μεγαλορήμονα, ‘big-talking’. Only here (grep). It answers ‘Linguam nostram magnificábimus’ of 11:5 — magní- … magnificá-. Douay-Rheims ‘the tongue that speaketh proud things’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘a língua que fala com arrogância’.

options.label: a língua que fala grandezas
options.note: Ruling: both halves of magni-loqua heard (great / speaking), and ‘grandezas’ answers ‘Engrandeceremos’ of the next verse as the Latin’s magní- answers magnificá-. ‘Falar grandezas’ is not a set phrase, but it is heard at once as boasting.

options.label: a língua arrogante
options.note: One adjective for one; the speaking and the echo are lost.

options.label: a língua que fala com arrogância

forms.magniloquam: a língua que fala com arrogância

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Names the vice where the Latin names the talk; the echo with 11:5 is lost.

options.label: a língua que fala coisas soberbas

forms.magniloquam: a língua que fala coisas soberbas

options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘proud things’.

decisions.why: ‘Our lips are from us’ (the Greek παρ᾿ ἡμῶν ἐστιν, ‘are with us, ours’): they owe their speech to no one. The verse says ‘we / our’ four times (nostram, nostra, nobis, noster). Douay-Rheims ‘our lips are our own’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘somos donos dos nossos lábios’.

options.label: os nossos lábios são nossos
options.note: Ruling: Douay-Rheims’ sense, and the run of ‘nosso’ that the Latin has (a nossa língua, os nossos lábios são nossos, o nosso senhor). The paroxytone ‘nossos’ at the mediant.

options.label: os nossos lábios vêm de nós

forms.anobis: os nossos lábios vêm de nós

options.note: The preposition to the letter (a nobis); a verb supplied, and it can be heard of where the lips came from.

options.label: os nossos lábios nos pertencem
options.note: Idiomatic (the Diurnal’s ‘nossa bôca nos pertence’); a verb for a preposition.

decisions.why: The boasters ask who is lord over them: any master, and — by implication — the Lord. Latin speech makes no difference of case; the printed capital of DO is its convention for every Dóminus. Portuguese print must choose. Douay-Rheims ‘who is Lord over us?’ (capital); Matos Soares 1932 ‘quem é o nosso senhor?’ (lower case).

options.label: quem é o nosso senhor
options.note: Ruling: lower case, as Matos Soares 1932: the word is theirs, and it keeps both readings — no master at all, and so not the Lord either. A capital would make them name God. Heard aloud there is no difference.

options.label: quem é o nosso Senhor
options.note: The Latin print’s capital; it makes the question a denial of God by name.

decisions.latin: Propter misériam ínopum, et gémitum páuperum
decisions.why: propter → por causa de (glossary, working; Ps 118:154 took ‘pelo’). inops (ἀπό … πτωχῶν) and pauper (πενήτων) are two words in the Latin and the Greek, often paired (inops et pauper 73:21, 85:1; páuperi et ínopi 71:13; 34:10, 36:14, 112:7, 139:13 — 14 lines with inops, grep), beside egénus (6 lines, grep: 34:10, 40:2, 69:6, 81:3, 81:4, 108:22) and mendícus (39:18, 108:17). pauper → pobre; inops ‘without resources’ → ‘indigente’ (its noun inópia → indigência: 33:10, 43:24, 87:9, 106:41); ‘necessitado’ is left for egénus. miséria → miséria (in Brazil the word for destitution, which is the sense). Matos Soares 1932 ‘Em atenção à miséria dos desvalidos, e ao gemido dos pobres’.

options.label: Por causa da miséria dos indigentes,

forms.propter: Por causa da miséria dos indigentes,

options.note: Ruling: the glossary’s ‘por causa de’, and inops → ‘indigente’, proposed for the glossary. Long: the colon is six syllables over the Latin.

options.label: Pela miséria dos indigentes,
options.note: Three syllables shorter (‘pelo’ as in 118:154); ‘pela’ can be heard as ‘by means of’.

options.label: Por causa da miséria dos desvalidos,

forms.propter: Por causa da miséria dos desvalidos,

options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s noun: the helpless, which is the Latin’s sense by extension.

decisions.why: The Lord still speaking. ‘Ponam’ has no object in the Latin or the Greek (θήσομαι ἐν σωτηρίᾳ): whom he will set in salvation is left to the hearer — the poor of 11:6a, or (as the next colon’s ‘in eo’ may suggest) one man. salutáre → salvação (D6). Douay-Rheims supplies ‘him’ (‘I will set him in safety’); Matos Soares 1932 ‘os’ (‘Eu os porei em salvo’).

options.label: Porei na salvação
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s bare verb; no object is supplied, so neither ‘him’ nor ‘them’ is decided for the hearer (rule 2). To be tested on the blind reader: Portuguese ‘pôr’ wants an object, and the ear may stumble.

options.label: Eu o porei na salvação
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘him’: one man, as ‘in eo’ may point to.

options.label: Eu os porei na salvação
options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s plural: the poor of 11:6a.

options.label: Porei a salvo
options.note: The idiom ‘pôr a salvo’; loses salvação (D6).

decisions.why: fiduciáliter: ‘confidently’ (Lewis & Short, citing this verse); the Greek παρρησιάσομαι ἐν αὐτῷ is ‘I will speak / act boldly in him (or it)’. ‘in eo’ is open: in him (the man set in salvation) or in it (the salvation). Douay-Rheims ‘I will deal confidently in his regard’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘nisto procederei confiadamente’ (decides ‘it’).

options.label: nele agirei com confiança
options.note: Ruling: ‘nele’ is as open as ‘in eo’ (him or it); agere → agir (the future, not the banned imperative ‘agi’); the adverb said as Portuguese says it, and the verse ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: nele agirei confiadamente
options.note: One adverb for one (Matos Soares 1932’s adverb); six syllables of it.

options.label: nisto procederei com confiança
options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s ‘nisto’: decides ‘it’ where the Latin leaves ‘him’ open.

decisions.why: D26: elóquium is ‘o que dissestes’ in Ps 118; outside it, where it is a subject with a genitive, the psalm decides between the clause, ‘dito(s)’ and ‘palavra(s)’ and says why — and 17:31 (elóquia Dómini igne examináta) will follow. Here the word is a subject with a genitive, said twice, the second time as predicate: ‘the Lord’s utterances [are] pure utterances’ (τὰ λόγια κυρίου λόγια ἁγνά). No verbum or sermo in the psalm. castus: pure, chaste, holy (ἁγνός); Douay-Rheims ‘pure words’, Matos Soares 1932 ‘palavras sinceras’, the Diurnal (from the Hebrew) ‘palavras sinceras’. ‘puro’ is wanted for mundus (50:12 cor mundum) and purgátum follows in this very verse (‘purificada’).

options.label: Os ditos do Senhor são ditos castos

forms.eloquia: Os ditos do Senhor são ditos castos

options.note: Ruling for draft 1, to be tested on the readers: the noun D26 keeps available — a thing uttered — which keeps λόγιον apart from λόγος (D15’s test) and repeats as the Latin repeats. The clause cannot serve: ‘o que o Senhor disse’ cannot be said a second time as a predicate without breaking the figure. Known risk: in Ps 118 the stylist refused the plural ‘ditos’ eight times of eight (‘máximas’, ‘coleção de máximas’); here it has a genitive and an adjective, which may change the hearing.

options.label: As palavras do Senhor são palavras castas

forms.eloquia: As palavras do Senhor são palavras castas

options.note: D16’s named retreat, and what Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 have: the plain word, the repetition kept. Costs the λόγιον / λόγος distinction; in this psalm nothing else would be ‘palavra’.

options.label: O que o Senhor disse é casto

forms.eloquia: O que o Senhor disse é casto

options.note: D26’s clause. The Latin’s repetition (elóquia … elóquia) cannot be kept: refused under rule 2.

options.label: Os ditos do Senhor são ditos puros

forms.eloquia: Os ditos do Senhor são ditos puros

options.note: ‘Puro’, the plainer adjective; it is wanted for mundus, and purgátum → ‘purificada’ follows.

options.label: As palavras do Senhor são palavras sinceras

forms.eloquia: As palavras do Senhor são palavras sinceras

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (and the Diurnal). ‘Sincero’ is another word (sincérus).

decisions.latin: argéntum igne examinátum, probátum terræ purgátum séptuplum
decisions.why: Three participles (tried, proved, purged) and ‘séptuplum’. examináre: to weigh, to test (Lewis & Short; from examen, the tongue of a balance); probáre → provar (138:23 Proba me). The two verbs stand side by side in 65:10 (probásti nos, Deus: igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum), so they must stay two words. ‘terræ’ is open: the Greek δοκίμιον τῇ γῇ (‘an assay [for / in] the earth’), Douay-Rheims ‘purged from the earth’, Matos Soares 1932 ‘acendrada no crisol’ (an interpretation: a crucible of earth). The silver stands in apposition, with no ‘as’ (Douay-Rheims adds ‘as’). 17:31 ‘elóquia Dómini igne examináta’ repeats the first participle; the glossary keeps 118:140 ignítus apart from it.

options.label: prata examinada no fogo, provada, purificada da terra sete vezes

forms.examinatum: prata examinada no fogo, provada, purificada da terra sete vezes

options.note: Ruling: the three participles kept three (examinar / provar / purificar); ‘da terra’ where it can hang on either neighbour as ‘terræ’ does (Douay-Rheims’ ‘from the earth’ is the nearer hearing); apposition kept. Ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: prata provada no fogo, examinada, purificada da terra sete vezes

forms.examinatum: prata provada no fogo, examinada, purificada da terra sete vezes

options.note: ‘Provada no fogo’ is the idiom; but it gives provar to examináre, which 65:10 must keep apart from probáre.

options.label: prata purificada no fogo, acendrada no crisol, refinada sete vezes

forms.examinatum: prata purificada no fogo, acendrada no crisol, refinada sete vezes

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Refused: ‘no crisol’ interprets ‘terræ’ and none of the three verbs is the Latin’s.

decisions.latin: Tu, Dómine, servábis nos: et custódies nos
decisions.why: Glossary: custodíre → guardar (working); serváre → observar (open, of a law), whose row says that 11:8, with persons as object and custodíre beside it, decides locally. The Greek has φυλάξεις … διατηρήσεις. Two Latin verbs, two Portuguese. Douay-Rheims ‘wilt preserve us: and keep us’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘nos guardarás, e nos preservarás’. The mediant falls after the second verb, as in the Latin.

options.label: nos conservareis: e nos guardareis
options.note: Ruling: custodíre keeps the glossary’s ‘guardar’; serváre with a person is ‘conservar’ — the verb of the everyday blessing ‘Deus vos conserve’; ‘observar’ cannot take a person.

options.label: nos preservareis: e nos guardareis
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘preserve’; ‘preservar de’ fits ‘a generatióne hac’, but it would belong to the second verb, not the first.

options.label: nos guardareis: e nos preservareis
options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s order; it gives ‘guardar’ to serváre, against the glossary.

decisions.why: altitúdo: height (and depth); of persons, loftiness (Lewis & Short); the Greek τὸ ὕψος σου. The Greek verb that follows, ἐπολυώρησας, is ‘you have held in high regard’; the Latin read ‘multiplicásti’, and the Latin is followed (rule 1). Douay-Rheims ‘according to thy highness’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘segundo o teu altíssimo desígnio’ (explains). Other places concrete: 68:3 altitúdinem maris, 94:4 altitúdines móntium, 102:11 altitúdinem cæli.

options.label: altura
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s concrete word, which the other places (102:11 ‘segundo a altura do céu’) will want too.

options.label: alteza
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘highness’. Refused: ‘Vossa Alteza’ is a royal title in Portuguese.

options.label: grandeza
options.note: Plainer of God; it is magnitúdo’s (glossary) and loses the height.

choices.11:2: The psalm begins at 11:2 (11:1 is the titulus; D7). Salvum me fac → ‘Salvai-me’ (glossary; the formula recurs 3:7, 6:5, 7:2, 68:2, 108:26, 117:25, 118:94, 146). The Latin’s two ‘quóniam’ kept as two ‘porque’. fílii hóminum → ‘filhos dos homens’ (glossary).
choices.11:4: univérsus → ‘todo’ (glossary, Ps 8). ‘lábios enganadores’ as in 11:3 (one decision fills both).
choices.11:5: Qui dixérunt → ‘Os que disseram’: a relative hung on the people of 11:4, as the Latin’s. magnificáre → engrandecer (glossary): ‘Engrandeceremos a nossa língua’ — the boast in the Latin’s own image (Matos Soares 1932 explains it: ‘Faremos grandes coisas com a nossa língua’).
choices.11:6a: The Lord speaks from here to the end of 11:6b. exsúrgere → levantar-se (glossary): ‘agora me levantarei, diz o Senhor’. D17 (address follows the speaker) is not engaged: he speaks of himself and addresses no one. gémitus → gemido (glossary).
choices.11:7: séptuplum → ‘sete vezes’ (Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932); 78:12 has séptuplum as a noun (‘sete vezes mais’) and decides there.
choices.11:8: Tu, Dómine → ‘Vós, Senhor’ (D1). in ætérnum → ‘para sempre’ (D23). ‘a generatióne hac’ → ‘desta geração’: guarded from this generation, as the Latin.
choices.11:9: in circúitu → ‘ao redor’, with no ‘de nós’ (Matos Soares 1932 adds it). ambuláre → andar (glossary). The Latin reads ‘multiplicásti’ where the Greek ἐπολυώρησας means ‘held in high regard’: the Latin is followed (rule 1).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm11.txt, nine prayed verses with DO’s ids (11:2–11:5, 11:6a, 11:6b, 11:7–11:9). 11:5 has a flex and a mediant; every other verse one ‘*’. 11:1 is the titulus (D7). Douay-Rheims from Bolls’ chapter 12 (= Vulgate Ps 11, checked by the coordinator).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps011.md. Sense from the Vulgate family (Douay-Rheims; Matos Soares 1932 by its text layer). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 has the psalm, made from the Hebrew: diction only — its sense refused where it follows the Hebrew (11:6b ‘darei salvação a quem deseje’, 11:9 ‘revelam-se péssimos homens’). DO’s Portuguese not used (D12). Lewis & Short read for fiducialiter, magniloquus, examino, altitudo. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: Salvum me fac (13 lines); defécit (8 lines, the glossary’s ‘desfalecer’ fails here); inops (14 lines) and egénus (6); lábia dolósa 16:1b, 30:18; elóquium (27 lines; 17:31 elóquia Dómini igne examináta is this verse’s twin); probáre and examináre side by side in 65:10; in salutári (7 lines); altitúdo (6); multiplicásti (4). No vós imperative in the psalm but ‘Salvai-me’ (safe: past ‘salvei’). Septuagintal readings kept against the Hebrew: 11:3 in corde et corde (the Hebrew idiom, word for word), 11:6b Ponam in salutári: fiduciáliter agam in eo, 11:7 probátum terræ, 11:9 secúndum altitúdinem tuam multiplicásti. D26 applied: elóquia decided locally (decision eloquia), to be tested.
